### Fixed

- `omo remote devices` shows this device offline while its device service is not connected, and `omo remote sessions --device` naming a device the account does not have reports it instead of listing nothing. ([#13916](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13916))
- Memory sync's own test suite no longer fails a later, unrelated test when one test times out while a sync cycle is still running: device teardown in the tests now stops the engine and waits for that cycle before removing its files, and the push-bounded test waits on the cycle instead of a fixed 30 s budget. ([#13887](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13887), fixes [#13680](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13680))
- The first memory sync cycle after signing in no longer fails with "the device's sign-in token could not be read or refreshed" when the system keychain briefly reads nothing. That one empty read is now checked again before sync treats the sign-in as gone; signing out still stops sync at once. ([#13879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13879), fixes [#13739](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13739))
- Regenerating the computer-use prelude (`bun run generate` in `senpi-desktop-prelude`) now runs its generated method tables through `bun fmt`, so `prelude.js`, its `index.ts` allowlist and the desktop protocol tier tables stay formatter-clean instead of reverting to unformatted output at every release regeneration. The published prelude JavaScript is the formatted copy again. ([#13855](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13855))

### Changed

- A memory sync capture that receives files from other devices no longer scans every known file once per received file, so a large memory catching up on many incoming files stays fast. ([#13862](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13862))

**A secret input or grant approval that settled while the relay link was down is now dismissed on the terminal that raised it after `omo remote attach` reconnects**, instead of staying open with an answer the session would refuse. ([#13773](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13773))

**The computer-use conformance preflight test cleans up its compiled stand-in engine reliably on Windows.** The test's temporary directory is now removed with the shared retrying helper, because Windows briefly keeps a just-run executable locked and Bun ignores `rmSync`'s retry options. QA tooling only; no runtime behaviour changes. ([#13299](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13299), part of #13221)

### Fixed

- The EQ.omo driver resolves a symlinked temp dir before it makes its sandboxes, so a recording on macOS no longer carries `/private<sandbox>` paths or an untrusted project. A new test fails when a platform's EQ.omo goldens were recorded with a senpi version more than a week away from the pinned one. ([#13865](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13865))
- CI: the desktop-bench comparison summary prints its regression thresholds (x1.3 and +0.5 ms) instead of `undefined`. It now reads them from `compareBench`'s result rather than destructuring names `eval-core.mjs` does not export. ([#13838](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13838), follow-up to #12876 review L1, [#12567](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12567))
- `omo remote bootstrap` installs device service 0.1.39 instead of 0.1.27, which was older than the wake and delivery minimum and answered open/create to the device with `unsupported`. ([#13803](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13803))
- A wake toward a device service older than the wake minimum now names the service's version, the minimum and the fix, instead of a bare `unsupported`. ([#13803](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13803))
- `omo remote devices` lists the device it runs on first (the account roster held only the other devices), and `--json` marks each row `this_device`. `omo remote sessions --device` with a device that is not on the account now fails with exit 2 naming it, instead of printing an empty list. ([#13458](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13458), part of [#13402](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13402))
- `thread_interrupt` also stops the background jobs the interrupted turn started (a bash command it ran in the background or that auto-detached), so the thread no longer wakes a minute later when that job ends and replies as if it had never been interrupted. The result names what was stopped as `background: { status: "stopped", stopped, failed }`; an engine that predates the stop answers `background: { status: "not_supported" }`. A thread on this device and a thread on another device run the same interrupt code and answer the same shape. ([#13444](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13444))
- Computer use v3 (fake backend): the source guard that bans environment reads now also reports a grouped `use std::{...}` import of the environment module when a `//` or `/* */` comment comes before the item inside the group. A comment can no longer hide an item, or split one at a comma or brace inside it. ([#13363](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13363))
- Desktop engine: the client retries a connection reset before the first reply byte only on Unix sockets, never on a Windows named pipe, where the daemon may already have run the request. ([#12744](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12744))

### Changed

- The `thread_read` wait limit (600,000 ms) is now internal to the thread schema instead of an unused export; the limit itself is unchanged. No behavior change. ([#13864](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13864))
- Internal: the Windows backend documents when its posted key rou

**Remote session views stop receiving each streamed delta twice.** `open_session` for a remote create, open, or fork now goes on the endpoint dialer (a fresh connection per call, closed once it settles), instead of sharing the long-lived connection the later `session.attach` rides on; opening on the shared connection had attached the host's delegated engine connection to the session as well, so the engine wrote every delta twice. A connection a caller lends is now named borrowed, so the CLI's one shared connection survives the open. ([#13761](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13761), adopting [#13075](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13075) by @surlymochan)

**The first session on a newly enabled device now starts memory sync.** Sync used to start before the memory repository existed, fail to write its space binding, log "memory sync failed to start" and never retry; it now waits for the repository and starts on its own once the first memory write creates it. ([#13493](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13493), fixes #13486) ([#13627](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13627))

**Memory sync drops a replaced desktop account cleanly.** When the desktop moved to another account without announcing a retirement, the engine opened the new account but left the old one half alive: it kept listening on the desktop channel and its open sync sessions did not end. The old account now ends as soon as the engine sees it is no longer current, which also ends its sessions. In a session Worker, an operation started just before the desktop retired its account can no longer hand back a handle from the old account. ([#13334](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13334), follow-up to #13327 and #13329) ([#13627](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13627))

OmO is ready to load on the tool side of a split session: its first-paint startup gate is declared for the agent-loop side, so the tool side never registers those handlers, and on the tool side deferred startup work runs right away instead of waiting for a paint that never comes; local sessions register exactly as before. ([#12329](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12329)) ([#13627](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13627))

Computer use is ready for the tool side of a split session: foreground control is revoked, and the engine session ended, when the run of the session holding it ends or that session closes, through that session's own lifecycle instead of loop events; local sessions behave exactly as before. ([#12328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12328)) ([#13627](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13627))

Adds the executable proof that computer use returns one screenshot per tool call, under today's capture caps and unchanged across the tool side of a split session; no behavior change. ([#12337](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12337)) ([#13627](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13627))

Computer use is ready for the tool side of a split session: there, foreground control follows the device's own exec setting (refused until exec is enabled on that device, then granted to any session without a per-session confirm); local sessions keep today's confirm exactly. ([#12332](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12332)) ([#13627](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13627))

Computer use is ready for the tool side of a split session: sessions sharing one device take its foreground one at a time, and only the holder can release it; local sessions behave exactly as before. ([#12339](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12339)) ([#13627](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13627))

Computer use is ready for the tool side of a split session: a missing OS permission (Screen Recording, Accessibility) raised there is re

**A thread send now reaches a session that is not running, on this device or on another of your devices, and starts it.** It needs senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (omo pins it), and device service 0.1.31 or later on both devices for a wake from another device. A reply to a sender on another device reads only that device's sessions instead of the whole account listing; a send to a live session that is paused or holds a Stop answers `queued` with `waiting_on: { kind: "hold", device }`; and `waiting_on.kind` in a `thread_send` result can be `approval`, `hold` or `wake`. ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))

### Changed

- `omo remote enable` now sets the device up in one command after `omo login`. It installs the OmO device service when none runs, registers this omo's agent dir with it, turns remote sessions on, and installs and starts the always-on session host unit. If you signed in before the device service was installed, it also links that sign-in to the service, so `omo login` then `omo remote enable` leaves the device connected. Running it again changes nothing that is already in place (#13594). ([#13602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13602)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- `omo remote status` also shows this device's own units as the service manager reports them: the session host unit (running, enabled, pinned host), the device service's unit, whether the cold-wake entry is in place, and the agent dir omo registers. With `--json` these are a `local` object beside the status fields (#13594). ([#13602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13602)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- Thread gateway: waking a session that is not running is on (#13037). It runs on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (omo now pins it), the release whose session release drops a woken session's retained record. A message from another of your devices wakes a session here once both devices run device service 0.1.31 or later. The local omo daemon (`omo daemon run`, or the device service's cold-wake unit) registers this device's agent dir with the device service and takes deliveries as soon as it starts, with no session open. ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the operator daemon declares the delivery consumer as soon as it loads omo, with no session open (#13037 cold wake). `omo daemon run` sends the daemon it ensured senpi's `warm`, so a daemon the device service starts on demand can be handed deliveries before any session runs. A warm that is refused or unsupported prints one line and the run still exits 0. ([#13596](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13596)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the session wake loads from its own sidecar (`extensions/omo-wake.js` behind `#omo-wake-runtime`): the carrier, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main `omo.js` bundle, which carries only lazy shells; the ensured host's idle-exit setting is read inside the sidecar. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: waking a session that is not running needs no setting (#13037). A `thread_send` from this machine to a session here that is not running now starts it by default, and the answer is `queued` with `waiting_on: { kind: "wake" }`. `session_wake.same_device` stays in the configuration schema only as an explicit opt-out (`false`), read for the target session's own project. The wake starts on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (senpi#6449), which omo now pins. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: when no operator host is running, a session that

The builtin `architect` category now defaults to Claude Fable 5.2 at thinking level `xhigh` instead of `max`: both chain rungs (the 5.2 lead and the 5.1 fallback, kept as the fallback at the same effort) carry `xhigh`, verified against the engine model catalog per the #9378 rule. Docs that spell the builtin default follow. Other categories, agent chains, and model profiles are unchanged (#13543). ([#13545](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13545)) ([#13563](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13563))

**Memory sync names the last unexplained "authority is unavailable" causes, and its log stays free of memory text.** When closing a sync operation, releasing its claim, or the request handler itself failed, Settings still showed the bare "Memory sync authority is unavailable." with nothing in the log. These now carry a code (`close_failed`, `release_failed`, `handler_failed`) and log a warning. Logged errors name the error type, not its message; only a sync service error keeps its service code and status, because other messages can quote memory content. A device or pending-request read whose failure returns after the service refused a request is logged again. Carried by the next train top's bundle regeneration. ([#13332](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13332), follow-up to #13157) ([#13563](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13563))

**A signed-out desktop no longer looks like a memory-sync error to the engine.** When the desktop had no signed-in account, the engine's main thread treated the desktop's refusal as a broken channel and the sync runner reported an error; it now reads it as signed out, as session Workers already did, and picks up the account once you sign in. Carried by the next train top's bundle regeneration. ([#13329](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13329), follow-up to #13325) ([#13563](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13563))

**Memory sync keeps working when you sign out and back in on the desktop.** Signing out and signing in again (with the same or another account) while the engine runs used to leave Settings > Memory > Sync on "Memory sync authority is unavailable." until the engine restarted. The engine now ends only the old account when the desktop retires it, ends that account's open sync sessions once, and picks up the new account on the next status read. It needs a desktop that keeps the private channel open across the rollover; with an older desktop the behaviour is unchanged. Carried by the next train top's bundle regeneration. ([#13327](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13327), fixes #13325) ([#13563](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13563))

**`omo remote` accepts `--` to end its options.** `omo remote send <device>/<session> -- --text that starts with dashes` now sends that text, and the same works for a model id given to `omo remote model`; before, any argument starting with `--` was refused as an unknown option. Options before `--` still apply. ([#13496](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13496), fixes #13431)

**The `omo remote` reference matches the command again.** It lists `open`, `send`, `model`, `interrupt` and `close` with their flags, and describes `attach` as a view you can type into; it no longer says the attach view is observe-only. The Senpi plugin README lists all 27 skills it ships (it said 19). ([#13492](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13492), fixes #13433)

**`omo remote --help` and `omo remote <command> --help` now answer.** They print the usage (or that command's entry with its flags) on stdout and exit 0, before any sign-in or device-service check, instead of failing as an unknown argument. `omo --help` lists `remote` among the commands. `-h` now also answers as a help flag after any verb, including in a value position (for example `omo remote open dev --project --help` prints help instea
